A.explanation: With $L = 100\text{ cm}$, $\lambda = 50\text{ cm}$ gives $L = 2\lambda$, which is an integer number of half-wavelengths and so fits antinodes at both open ends.

B.explanation: With $\lambda = 75\text{ cm}$, $L/\lambda = 100/75 = 1.33$ is not a multiple of $0.5$, so antinodes cannot form at both open ends.

C.explanation: With $\lambda = 150\text{ cm}$, $L/\lambda = 100/150 = 0.67$ is not a multiple of $0.5$, so it does not satisfy the open-open pipe condition.

D.explanation: With $\lambda = 300\text{ cm}$, $L/\lambda = 100/300 = 0.33$ is less than $0.5$, so not even the fundamental half-wavelength fits in the $100\text{ cm}$ pipe.

hints: Notice the pipe is open at both ends, so the air displacement must have an antinode at each end of the $100\text{ cm}$ length.
Recall the open-open condition that the length must contain a whole number of half-wavelengths: $L = n\lambda/2$.
Test each listed wavelength in $cm$ by checking if $100/\lambda$ is a multiple of $0.5$.
walkthrough: Identify the boundary condition: for a pipe open at both ends, there is a displacement antinode at each open end.
State the stationary wave rule for this pipe: length $L$ must equal an integer number $n$ of half-wavelengths, $L = n\lambda/2$, where $n = 1, 2, 3...$.
Rearrange for allowed wavelengths with $L = 100\text{ cm}$: $\lambda = 2L/n = 200/n\text{ cm}$.
Check the options: $50\text{ cm} = 200/4\text{ cm}$ with $n = 4$, while $75\text{ cm}$, $150\text{ cm}$ and $300\text{ cm}$ do not give an integer $n$.
Therefore $50\text{ cm}$ fits two full wavelengths with antinodes at both ends. This is option A.
